scenes.title: the wrong answer
scenes.place: a paper table with a phone on it
scenes.summary: The film opens on the question: if Uber does not own the cars, what does it own?

visual.subject: a paper city map joining rider and driver nodes into a network

scenes.title: the match
scenes.place: a rider's phone, a driver's car, a city corridor
scenes.summary: A rider taps, a driver moves, and the platform puts the two together.

visual.subject: a phone map with a rider pin, a driver pin and a car on the route
visual.setting: a rider's phone and a paper city street
visual.action: a thumb taps, the route draws, the car moves

scenes.title: the cut
scenes.summary: The fare is divided: the driver keeps the rest, Uber keeps the service fee.

visual.subject: a fare bar split into a driver share and a small service fee, then coins moving
visual.action: the fare splits and the coins divide

scenes.title: more than a fare
scenes.place: the same app, four other doors
scenes.summary: Delivery, freight, advertising and memberships turn one network into several revenues.

visual.subject: one phone with four revenue tiles and two city routes crossing
visual.setting: the app and the city it serves
visual.action: tiles land, delivery and freight routes cross

scenes.title: the loop
scenes.place: a city of small paper doors
scenes.summary: More riders make each car busier; more drivers shorten the wait; the network gets harder to leave.

visual.subject: a denser network of rider and driver nodes with a shrinking wait bar
visual.action: nodes multiply and the wait shortens
